content.title: UCLA, South Carolina to meet for women's NCAA championship
content.text: April 3, 2026Updated April 5, 2026, 11:07 a.m. MTThe women's national championship will feature South Carolina and UCLA after the NCAA Tournament semifinals concluded on April 3 in Phoenix.After South Carolina defeated UConn earlier in the night, the UCLA Bruins punched their ticket to the title game.Kiki Rice made a pair of free throws with 3 seconds left to seal the 51-44 win.UCLA was led by Lauren Betts with 16 points and 11 rebounds. Kiki Rice (11 points), Gianna Kneepkens (10) and Gabriela Jaquez (10) each finished in double digits.UCLA pulled down 30 defensive rebounds.Kyla Oldacre led Texas with 11 points off the bench. The Longhorns shot 31% from the floor and just 22% from 3.Women's national championship game picks: South Carolina vs UCLA | The Republic's score prediction | Win probabilitiesWomen's national championship game odds: South Carolina vs UCLA | Betting oddsHow to watch women's national championship game: South Carolina vs UCLA | Schedule | TV channels | Announcers Texas trails by 3Layups by Kyla Oldacre and Jordan Lee helped cut UCLA's lead from 10 to 3.The Texans are fighting to extend their season one more game to face South Carolina for the national championship.Score: UCLA 47, Texas 44 (0:55 Q4) Lauren Betts' jumper keeps UCLA up 10Each time Texas attempts to cut into UCLA's lead, someone makes a shot for the Bruins.Lately, that's been Lauren Betts, who has 16 points and 10 rebounds.Score: UCLA 47, Texas 37 (2:41 Q4) UCLA back up by 10As quickly as Texas cut into the lead, UCLA re-established it.Lauren Betts made a pair of free throws, then assisted on a 3 by Kiki Rice.A steal set up a Gabriela Jaquez layup before the Longhorns tried to stop the damage with a timeout.Score: UCLA 38, Texas 28 (8:30 Q4) Texas forces UCLA timeoutA free throw by Justice Carlton cut UCLA's lead to 3 with less than a minute left in the third.The Bruins led 29-21 less than a minute earlier. That was before Carlton made a pair of jumpers.Score: UCLA 29, Texas 28 (0:40 Q3)Watch Women's Final Four games on FUBO (free trial) Madison Booker's struggles continue for Texas vs UCLAMadison Booker is now 1-for-16 in this game.She has missed 15 straight attempts since making his first shot attempt of the game.If Texas wants a chance to get back in this game, it is going to need her to obviously get some buckets.Score: UCLA 28, Texas 21 (3:30 left in third quarter) Madison Booker fouls Lauren Betts hard in Women's Final FourA scary moment in this game happened when Texas star Madison Booker ran into UCLA star Lauren Betts.Betts hit her head on the court as she fell down. Booker was showing holding her leg.Booker was called for a foul on the play. The officials reviewed the play to see if it met the criteria for a flagrant foul, but did not assess a flagrant on Booker.Score: UCLA 22, Texas 19 (7:19 left in third quarter) UCLA clinging to lead against Texas at Women's Final FourIt's pretty remarkable that Texas is this close against UCLA.The Longhorns are now 9-for-34 from the field. Madison Booker is 1-for-13.And they only trail by three points at the Women's Final Four.Kyla Oldacre has six points off the bench to help Texas.Score: UCLA 22, Texas 19 (7:41 left in third quarter) UCLA leads Texas at half of Women's Final FourTexas scored just six points in the first quarter of the Women's Final Four game against UCLA.UCLA scored just six points in the second quarter against Texas.The Bruins have a 20-17 halftime lead in an ugly game at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix.Texas is just 8-for-32 from the field. UCLA is 9-for-24.Gianna Kneepkens leads UCLA with seven points, while Rori Harmon has a game-high eight for Texas.Madison Booker has just two points on 1-for-12 shooting for the Longhorns. Lauren Betts has six points for UCLA.Halftime score: UCLA 20, Texas 17 Rori Harmon coming up big for Texas vs UCLAAmid all the offensive woes for Texas, Rori Harmon has been a bright spot.She is now 4-for-6 from the field with a game-high eight points, which has helped Texas get back in this game amid a woeful shooting night (the Longhorns are just 8-for-30 from the field as a team).Score: UCLA 20, Texas 17 (1:16 left in second quarter) Madison Booker, Texas struggling offensively against UCLAPoints have been hard to come by in this second Women's Final Four game.Especially for Texas.The Longhorns have just eight points in this game. They are 4-for-20 from the field.After hitting her first attempt, Madison Booker has missed eight shots in a row for Texas.Can Texas get something going against UCLA?Score: UCLA 16, Texas 8 (6:42 left in second quarter) UCLA takes 8-point lead on Texas at end of first quarterUCLA has held Texas to a season low for points in a quarter as the Longhorns only scored six points in the first 10 minutes of the game.Texas is just 3-for-14 from the field. Madison Booker is 1-for-6 from the field for the Longhorns.The Bruins were led by Gianna Kneepkens' five points in the first. UCLA holds an early 11-7 edge in rebounds.Score: UCLA 14, Texas 6 (end of first quarter) UCLA builds 10-point lead vs Texas in first quarterUCLA handed Texas its largest deficit of the tournament went Angela Dugalic made a 3 to put UCLA up 12-4.It then added to it with a driving layup by Gabriela Jaquez, which put the Bruins up 14-4.UCLA couldn't have dreamed of a better start against Texas, which is now just 2-for-9 from the field.The Longhorns haven't scored since there was 6:26 left in the first.Score: UCLA 14, Texas 4 (2:08 left in first quarter) UCLA out to early lead vs Texas in Women's Final Four gameThe Bruins have the early advantage on the Longhorns in the second Women's Final Four national semifinal game at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix.Gianna Kneepkens and Lauren Betts have all nine points for the Bruins, who had a 7-0 run after falling behind 2-0.Texas is shooting just 2-for-6 from the field. UCLA is 4-for-9.Score: UCLA 9, Texas 4 (4:29 left in first quarter) What time is Texas vs UCLA Women's Final Four game?The UCLA vs Texas Women's Final Four game is set to tip-off at 6:40 p.m. MST (9:40 p.m. ET) on ESPN. Texas vs UCLA up next in Women's Final FourWe know one half of the women's national championship game after South Carolina ended UConn's 54-game win streak with a 62-48 win over the Huskies in the first national semifinal.But who will the Gamecocks play in the title game on Sunday in Phoenix?We don't have to wait long to find out.No. 1 seed Texas and No. 1 seed UCLA are up next at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, with the winner advancing to face South Carolina. South Carolina beats UConn, advances to championshipStrong rebounding by South Carolina and poor shooting by the Huskies was the recipe the Gamecocks needed for a 62-48 victory over UConn in the women's basketball semifinals.South Carolina advances to the championship game, where it will face either Texas or UCLA.Ta'Niya Latson led South Carolina with 16 points and 11 rebounds. She was 10-for-10 from the free-throw line.Joyce Edwards added 11 points and 8 rebounds for the Gamecocks, who outrebounded UConn 47-32.UConn (38-1) saw its bid for an undefeated season end. The Huskies shot just 29% from beyond the arc and 31% from the floor. They entered the game shooting 39.6% from 3 and 52.5% from the floor.Sarah Strong led UConn with a double-double of 12 points and 12 rebounds. Time running out on UConnUConn's hope of an undefeated season is fading.The Huskies trail 55-47 with 1:45 to play. South Carolina holding onto leadEach time the Huskies have started to close in, a South Carolina player has come up with a big shot.Agot Makeer was the latest when she drained a 3 with 5:52 play, which gave the Gamecocks a 51-44 lead.UConn cut the game to two at 46-44, but South Carolina took off again. Sarah Strong dons No. 55UConn's Sarah Strong has switched from No. 21 to No. 55 after her jersey ripped.Video of Strong appears to show her ripping her own jersey.The game has turned physical with 10 fouls called in the third quarter — all of them against UConn. UConn closes the gapAfter trailing by as many as 10 points in the third quarter, the Huskies have charged back. They now trail South Carolina 42-39 with 31 seconds left in the half. South Carolina makes a runUConn has called a timeout in an attempt to stop a 12-2 run by the Gamecocks.South Carolina leads 36-28 with 5:24 left in the third quarter. UConn leads South Carolina at halftimeSouth Carolina is outrebounding UConn 24-16, but the Huskies have the 26-24 lead on the scoreboard.UConn is shooting just 13% (1-for-8) from 3, but is 40% (12-for-30) from the floor.UConn's Sarah Strong and Ashley Shade lead all players with 8 points each. Strong has 6 rebounds. Offensive rebounds fueling GamecocksSouth Carolina leads 21-20 with 4:28 left in the first half.The team has 9 offensive rebounds and 10 defensive rebounds. UConn has a total of 11 rounds.Joyce Edwards, Tessa Johnson and Ta'Niya Latson have each scored 6 points for South Carolina. UConn, South Carolina tied after first quarterAgot Makeer hit a 3-pointer with 3 seconds left in the first quarter and tied the game at 15-all. Makeer leads the Gamecocks with 5 points.The Huskies led by as many as 5 points.Sarah Strong leads UConn with 5 points. UConn first to get separationThe Huskies were the first to get an edge. It came 13-8 lead with 3:27 to play in the first quarter and prompted the Gamecocks to call a timeout.It's been a balanced effort for UConn with Sarah Strong (5 points), Serah Williams (4) and Ashlynn Shade (4) accounting for the scoring. Final Four atmosphereUConn fans have clearly made their presence known outside the arena. People all across the country have made their way out to the Valley in order rally behind the Huskies.Behind UConn, the South Carolina fans have been trickling in, with many of the fans wearing shirts supporting their coach, Dawn Staley.Meanwhile, some UCLA alumni rented out TOM’S Watch Bar as a place to rally some Bruins fans before the Bruins take on the Longhorns in the second game of the night.Crawford Clark was born and raised in Columbia, South Carolina, where the Gamecocks call home. Clark is committed to never missing an opportunity to watch his team play.“Being a retired military veteran, no matter where I was deployed, I was always looking for a place to watch the Gamecocks play,” he said. Clark is vocal about what Dawn Staley has done in keeping this team glued together.“She’s had a rough year this year, with Chloe Kitts going down, Dawn has taken it upon herself to mold the team and keep them working as a cohesive unit,” Clark said. UConn and South Carolina countdown underwayAs both teams hit the court just after 2 p.m. to get up some shots, the media and customer specialists at Mortgage Matchup Center were busy. Seating charts, Final Four towels for every seat.And the "Probable Starting Lineups" landed.UConn (38-0): Head coach Geno AuriemmaNo. 2 KK Arnold, 5-9 junior guard from Germantown, Wisconsin.No. 12 Ashlynn Shade, 5-10 junior guard from Noblesville, IndianaNo. 21 Sarah Strong, 6-2 sophomore guard from Durham, North CarolinaNo. 22 Serah Williams, 6-4 senior forward from Brooklyn, New YorkNo. 35 Azzi Fudd, 5-11 graduate guard from Arlington, VirginiaSouth Carolina (35-3): Head coach Dawn StaleyNo. 0 Ta'Niya Latson, 5-9 senior guard from Miami, FloridaNo. 5 Tessa Johnson, 6-0 junior guard from Albertville, MinnesotaNo. 8 Joyce Edwards, 6-3 sophomore forward from Camden, South CarolinaNo. 11 Madina Okot, 6-6 senior center from Mumias, KenyaNo. 25 Raven Johnson, 5-9 senior guard from Atlanta, Georgia What time is the Texas vs UCLA Women's Final Four game?The UCLA vs Texas Women's NCAA Tournament Final Four game is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. MST (9:30 p.m. ET) on Friday, April 3.How to watch Women's Final Four: South Carolina vs UConn | Texas vs UCLA | UConn vs South Carolina TV | UCLA vs Texas TV | Schedule | TV channels | Game times | Announcers | Who is in Final Four? | Final Four tickets What channel is the UCLA vs Texas Women's Final Four game on?The Texas vs UCLA Women's Final Four NCAA Tournament game can be seen on ESPN.
